notes: US name 'motorola razr ultra - 2026' and global name 'motorola razr 70 ultra' are ONE physical device, stated by Motorola: the April 29, 2026 press release pairs 'the new motorola razr ultra – 2026' (United States) with 'motorola razr 70 ultra ... in Europe, Middle East, Africa, Latin America, and Asia-Pacific'. Corroborated by identical geometry on motorola.com/us (pmipmjk44m3) and motorola.com/gb (pmipmjk44m2): 88.12 × 73.99 × 15.69 closed, 171.48 × 73.99 × 7.19 open, 199 g. Motorola labels these 'H x W x D' itself. MAIN DIAGONAL: 6.96" is taken from Motorola Support US a_id 192853 and the GB product page; motorola.com/us rounds the same panel to '7.0"' in its Display Size field and the press release says '7.0" Extreme AMOLED'. The precise figure is kept per the spec's precision rule; both are Motorola's. Resolutions recorded [width, height] as Motorola prints them ('1224 x 2992', '1272 x 1080'); no orientation is stated for the cover panel. Cover glass differs by region and both variants are recorded verbatim. materials.back are the two published finishes (Alcantara for PANTONE Orient Blue, wood veneer for PANTONE Cocoa). free_stop true from the press release Flex View statement and the product page copy ('With Flex View and an AI-powered camera system'). crease null: Motorola never states a crease shape - note that a marketing video asset on the GB page is named 'razr_70_ultra_creaseless', but a filename is not a specification and was not used. announced/released read from Motorola's press release via a web.archive.org snapshot dated 2026-05-21, because motorolanews.com returns HTTP 403 to direct fetching; May 21 is the US on-sale date. Motorola also publishes IP48 and a 5,000 mAh silicon-carbon battery for this model - no fields exist here for those. || EVIDENCE SWEEP 2026-09-13: these values were present in the research pass but carried NO sources[] entry covering their field, so they were set to null per the registry rule (a value without a citation is an assertion, not evidence). Preserved verbatim here so a human can re-source rather than re-research: hinge.type = 'flip'; hinge.axis = 'short'.
